newsitem.title: INDIA: India unveils measures to boost markets.
newsitem.headline: India unveils measures to boost markets.

text.p: Indian Finance Minister P. Chidambaram on Friday unveiled a package of tax relief and other measures aimed at boosting India's stock markets, which suffered after his federal budget in July.
But the package got an initial thumbs down from traders on markets, which had ended business for the week when Chidambaram spoke in parliament.
He exempted all investments in mutual funds from capital gains taxation and doubled the amount investors can borrow from banks against shares to one million rupees ($28,570).
Chidambaram also announced a package for the capital market while replying in parliament to a debate on the 1996/97 (April-March) budget.

He said he would discuss other tax proposals next week before a final vote on the budget presented by the centre-left coalition government, which came to power in June after indecisive general elections.

Chidambaram gave a boost to the bond market by permitting foreign institutional investors (FIIs), who represent pension funds and portfolio investors, to invest all of their funds in debt instruments.
To now, they were allowed to invest only 30 percent in debt instruments.
The government raised by 2,000 rupees to 15,000 the limit up to which annual income earned by investors in securities specified by the government would be exempt from income tax.
"The capital market is a place where almost 20 million Indians have invested their hard-earned savings," Chidambaram said.
"While speculation is an unavoidable feature of any market, we must impart a certain stability to our markets so that the interests of millions of small investors are protected," he added.
Chidambaram's statement was after the end of trading in India's 23 bourses.
Stocks ended lower in Bombay, the financial capital. The 30-stock Bombay sensitive index fell 8.83 points to 3,508.07 after hitting an early high of 3,543.21.
The index began a steady fall after the budget announcement on July 22. In the last pre-budget session the index stood at 3,797.85.
A major setback to traing after the budget was a minimum tax imposed on profits of companies earlier exempted from corporate taxes if they ploughed back profits into their businesses.
Initial market reaction to Chidambaram's speech on Friday was muted because he held off the main issue of a minimum tax on companies. He has been expected to relax the controversial tax.
"If these are the only incentives, the market will take a dive next week," Bombay broker Ramesh Damani told Reuters.
"The pace is slow, terribly slow but the direction is right," an analyst at a foreign brokerage said.
